correctness.rationale: Definition-1 exact EF for unit chores reduces to min(a_i,b_j)<=a_j for every source i including housekeeper and every agent j. An unsaturated agent a_j<b_j must be a global load maximum; all unsaturated agents have the same level t, every saturated agent has b_i<=t and h<=t. This proves precisely the all-full and water-level vectors a_i=min(b_i,t), 0<=t<max b_i. Multinomial counting of distinct assignments is exact and disjoint. The band I_t=[F(t),F(t)+t] has next-start increment R(t+1); R is nonincreasing, so the last missing interval ends at F(t_*)-1 and all subsequent work levels are covered. Handles m=0, n=2, B=1 and all-full. Independently enumerated small labelled assignment sets and matched formulas; not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Complete exact EF feasibility, all load vectors, labelled allocation census and sharp eventual workload cutoff for every integer capacity profile solve natural questions in a canonical budgeted fair-division model. The strict-Durfee last gap is a meaningful arithmetic boundary even when weaker EF1/EFX are always possible. Four budget-five agents have no exact EF with 11 chores, but 369600 labelled EF assignments with 12 and feasibility thereafter. Neither a textbook renaming nor an arbitrary finite table.
